method: Read retained native Worker spans through the signed-in Cloudflare dashboard. The API credential still lacks telemetry access. Fields below are transcribed from the displayed span details. No new registration or deployment was run.
result: The original 740 ms admission interval is a native d1_batch span containing four SQL statements. SQL execution totals 1.9632 ms. Native metadata places both Worker and D1 primary in Singapore. The platform exposes no child spans dividing D1 dispatch, queueing, or durable write acknowledgement.

attemptCountInterpretation.explanation: Cloudflare aggregateD1Meta adds total_attempts across statement results. Four attempts for a four-statement successful batch is consistent with one attempt per statement, not four retries. The instrumented sample independently reports [1,1,1,1].

limits: Native span timestamps equal the application timestamps here. They do not remove the clock-clamping limitation or provide an independent physical clock.
The caller span starts 84 ms after the child D1 span in the recorded timeline. Do not subtract parent and child durations to claim 5 ms of dispatch or network latency.
The original request was unmodified by our temporary observers. Its SQL and native timing metadata were retained by the existing platform instrumentation.
The original 740 ms span has no local storage-sync observation. That intervention belongs only to the later matched examples.
Grouped local SQL spans in the timeline cover repeated polling over an interval. Their displayed group duration is not cumulative SQL execution and is not additive to the D1 span.
correction: Earlier reports said the original 740 ms request had no SQL metadata. That was true of the captured live tail. Retained native tracing now supplies its SQL duration and aggregated attempt count.
latencyFixStatus: No runtime latency fix verified. The guarded update and coherent root/cancellation reads remain intact.
